patch.summary:
Thesis: Same category, different company size — Both sit in ecommerce, but documented company-size audiences diverge.

Comparison thesis: Same category, different company size. Choose Saleor only if your buying job matches “Headless GraphQL commerce — OSS self-host free; Cloud Select $1599/mo, Volume $3999/mo, En” rather than Wix's shape. Choose Wix only if your buying job matches “Website-first builder with ecommerce from Core — Light $17/mo annual, Core $29 (sell onlin” rather than Saleor's shape. Workflow advantage: Saleor leans shared coverage; Wix leans checkout-conversion, catalog-management. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Same category, different company size — Both sit in ecommerce, but documented company-size audiences diverge.
- Positioning: Saleor is Headless GraphQL commerce — OSS self-host free; Cloud Select $1599/mo, Volume $3999/mo, Enterprise quote. Forever Free is non-commercial onl; Wix is Website-first builder with ecommerce from Core — Light $17/mo annual, Core $29 (sell online), Business $39, Business Elite $159 (annual tile.
- Company-size focus: Saleor (mid-market, enterprise) vs Wix (solo, micro, small-business).
- Workflow coverage skew: Saleor-leaning — vs Wix-leaning checkout-conversion, catalog-management, website-builder-commerce.
- Researched limits: Saleor — Cloud Select floor ($1599/mo) is high versus WooCommerce hosting TCO; Wix — Website-builder commerce depth trails Shopify-class platforms on complex catalogs and B2B.

Limitations — Saleor: Cloud Select floor ($1599/mo) is high versus WooCommerce hosting TCO; Forever Free Cloud is non-commercial — not a production merchant free plan; Wix: Website-builder commerce depth trails Shopify-class platforms on complex catalogs and B2B; Plan gates for selling start at Core — Free/Light are not store plans.

Poor-fit cases: Saleor is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Cloud Select floor ($1599/mo) is high versus WooCommerce hosting TCO · Wix is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Website-builder commerce depth trails Shopify-class platforms on complex catalogs and B2B · Avoid Saleor if you actually need Wix's motion (Website-first builder with ecommerce from Core — Light $17/mo annual, Core $29 ()

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
